l1_trend_projection: Deaths within 30 days, Spain, 1993–2024 (road fuel from 1996), against segmented trends fitted up to 2019 and projected from 2020 with 95% prediction intervals; the trend per tonne of fuel is converted back into deaths. Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos.
l4_km_against_fuel: Interurban deaths within 30 days as a ratio to a trend fitted to 2008–2019 and projected from 2020, per measured vehicle-kilometre and, as a check on fuel as a measure of traffic, over the road fuel sold for every road in Spain, towns included, with the trend's 95% prediction range shaded, Spain, 2010–2023; the kilometres leave out roads run by municipalities and other bodies, which account for 8.7% to 11.2% of interurban deaths (2016–2024). Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos; Ministerio de Transportes y Movilidad Sostenible, Anuario Estadístico 2023.
m1_season_profile: Deaths within 30 days, road fuel sold (petrol plus diesel), petrol sold and toll-motorway traffic per kilometre by month, each divided by its year's mean month and averaged over 2014–2024 (2020, 2021 left out), Spain; petrol and toll motorways cover only part of all traffic, and toll traffic is a daily average where the other series are monthly totals. Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos; Ministerio de Transportes y Movilidad Sostenible, tráfico en autopistas estatales de peaje.
m2_month_effects: Deaths within 30 days in each month against the average month of the same year, per day of the month and per tonne of road fuel sold, Spain, 2014–2024 (2020, 2021 left out), with 95% intervals. Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos.
m3_lockdown: Change in deaths within 30 days and in road fuel sold (petrol plus diesel) in each month of 2020 against the mean of the same month in 2017–2019, Spain; the state of alarm began on 14 March 2020. Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024; CORES, consumo de productos petrolíferos.
a3_sex_ratios: Men's rates divided by women's among private-car drivers (taxis and ride-hailing cars excluded), by age: involvement in injury crashes and death within 30 days per licence holder, and death per driver involved, Spain, 2022–2024 pooled, with 95% intervals. The estimates per kilometre are given in the text. Source: DGT, Accidentes con víctimas, tablas estadísticas 2014–2024; DGT, Censo de conductores 2014–2025. n = 285,327 drivers involved.
f1_speed_severity: Deaths within 30 days per 100 injury crashes in which the police recorded inappropriate speed, as a ratio to the same rate in the other injury crashes on the same type of road, Spain outside Catalonia and the Basque Country, 2016–2023 pooled, with 95% intervals that allow for year-to-year variation (for the adjusted ratio, also for the differences between road types). Source: DGT, Informe temático Factor Velocidad 2014–2023; DGT, Ficheros de microdatos de accidentes con víctimas 2016–2024. n = 45,192 crashes with inappropriate speed recorded.
f2_factor_shares: Injury crashes in which the police recorded each factor, as a share of all injury crashes on interurban roads and on urban streets, Spain outside Catalonia and the Basque Country, 2014–2023; a line breaks, at a short vertical mark, where the share rises by more than 25% or falls by more than 20% in a year, or a year has fewer than 200 crashes. Source: DGT, Informe temático Factor Velocidad 2014–2023.
s1_forest_fatal: Odds ratios for at least one death in an injury crash, by crash circumstance, from a logistic regression that also includes the year, against reference levels (hollow markers), with 95% intervals, Spain, 2016–2024; zone and road type describe one location between them and are read together; levels that record a missing value are in the model but not drawn. Source: DGT, Ficheros de microdatos de accidentes con víctimas 2016–2024. n = 875,013 crashes.
dr1_involved_per_km: Car drivers involved in injury crashes in Spain in 2024 per kilometre driven, as ratios to drivers aged 45–64 (log scale), with 95% sampling intervals. The kilometres by age share out DGT's car kilometres with the average of the Barcelona and Madrid travel surveys' age profiles; at 65–74 and 75 and over they also use the Madrid survey's split of the 65-and-over kilometres. The range across alternative assumptions, which the intervals leave out: 18–29 2.7 (range 1.5–3.6); 30–44 1.2 (range 1.1–1.7); 65–74 1.1 (range 0.7–1.6); 75 and over 2.4 (range 0.9–3.1). Source: DGT, Accidentes con víctimas, tablas estadísticas 2014–2024; ATM, Idescat and Institut Metròpoli, Enquesta de mobilitat en dia feiner 2022–2024; CRTM, Encuesta Domiciliaria de Movilidad 2018 (Powered by CRTM); DGT, Kilómetros anualizados recorridos por el parque móvil 2024; INE, Estadística Continua de Población. n = 96,526 drivers involved.
dr2_killed_per_involved: Private-car drivers who died within 30 days per 1,000 involved in an injury crash, by age, Spain, 2024, with 95% intervals; no measure of driving enters the rate. Source: DGT, Accidentes con víctimas, tablas estadísticas 2014–2024. n = 96,526 drivers involved.
v1_per_vehicle_vs_per_km: Vehicles of each type involved in fatal crashes (deaths within 30 days) per 100,000 circulating vehicles (left) and per billion vehicle-kilometres (right), Spain, 2022. The vertical position shows the rank only; each rate is printed beside its point. Per kilometre only the lead of motorcycles is clear of the 95% intervals of the types below, some of which overlap (intervals and counts by type in the rates table). Source: DGT, Accidentes con víctimas, tablas estadísticas 2014–2024; DGT, Kilómetros recorridos estimados a partir de la ITV 2022. n = 2,374 vehicles in fatal crashes.
p1_points_series: Monthly road deaths within 30 days, Spain, January 2000 to November 2007 (top) and enlarged from January 2005 (bottom), with the fitted model, a segmented regression, and from 1 July 2006 two projections without the change: the preferred pre-trend (dashed) and a straight-line pre-trend (dotted), which gives the larger drop. The value axes do not start at zero. The projections are drawn without intervals; the intervals of the step and of the average change are given in the text and in the table of every specification. Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024. n = 38,852 deaths.
p2_july_placebos: Estimated change in the level of monthly deaths at 1 July 2006 and at every other July of 1998–2018 whose window avoids July 2006 and the pandemic, each from the same segmented regression on 60 months before and 17 after, Spain, with model-based 95% intervals, which these placebos show to be too narrow; the filled marker is July 2006. The Julys of 2005 and 2007–2011 are left out because their windows include July 2006. Source: DGT, Series históricas del Anuario de Accidentes 2024. n = 15 fits.
d1_missingness: Share of crashes with a value recorded in each field of the DGT crash records, among the crashes the field applies to, by year, Spain, 2016–2024. A value is not applicable, and is left out, when it is 998 (not applicable), when the road is 'No inventariada' (no road number) and when the island field is empty, which DGT's dictionary defines as not applicable. An empty cell in the fog or strong wind field counts as recorded, as the 'no' of a field filled in only when the condition was present. A value is missing when it is 999 (not specified), an explicit unknown code, a placeholder (kilometre post 9999, and 1000 in 2019; municipality 00000) or any other empty cell, although in the kilometre post field an empty cell may also mean there was nothing to record. The junction type, the right-of-way flags and the crossing road apply only at a junction and are not drawn. Source: DGT, Ficheros de microdatos de accidentes con víctimas 2016–2024. n = 875,013 crashes.
cat1_fatal_by_road: Fatal crashes as a share of crashes with a death or serious injury, by road type, Catalonia, 2010–2023, with 95% intervals; groups of fewer than 30 crashes are left out. Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury. n = 24,478 crashes.
cat2_fatal_by_speed_limit: Fatal crashes as a share of crashes with a death or serious injury, by posted speed limit (the limit signposted on the road, not a measured speed), Catalonia, 2010–2023, with 95% intervals; groups of fewer than 30 crashes are left out; 73% of the crashes have no posted limit recorded, and the generic limit for the type of road applied. Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury. n = 24,478 crashes.
cat3_fatal_by_unit: Fatal crashes as a share of crashes with a death or serious injury, by type of road user or vehicle involved, Catalonia, 2010–2023, with 95% intervals; groups of fewer than 30 crashes are left out. Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury. n = 24,478 crashes.
cat4_fatal_by_crash_type: Fatal crashes as a share of crashes with a death or serious injury, by crash type, Catalonia, 2010–2023, with 95% intervals; groups of fewer than 30 crashes are left out. Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury. n = 24,478 crashes.
bcn1_severity_by_road_user: People seriously or fatally injured as a share of the people in recorded crashes with a recorded injury outcome, by road-user role and vehicle type, Barcelona, 2025, with 95% intervals; groups of fewer than 30 people are left out. Source: Ajuntament de Barcelona, Guàrdia Urbana crash records. n = 15,848 people.
bcn2_severity_by_age: People seriously or fatally injured as a share of the people in recorded crashes with a recorded injury outcome, by age band, Barcelona, 2025, with 95% intervals; groups of fewer than 30 people are left out. Source: Ajuntament de Barcelona, Guàrdia Urbana crash records. n = 15,848 people.
bcn4_crash_severity_by_type: Crashes with at least one death or serious injury as a share of recorded crashes, by crash type, Barcelona, 2025, with 95% intervals; types of fewer than 30 crashes are left out. Source: Ajuntament de Barcelona, Guàrdia Urbana crash records. n = 7,741 crashes.
sev2_held_out: ROC-AUC of the Catalan severity model refitted without the crashes it is tested on (the last year from the years before it, each province in turn, Barcelona city from the rest of Catalonia), with 95% intervals, beside the same model fitted and cross-validated in the test population (hollow). The n beside each tested model is its number of test crashes. Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury.
sev1_predicted_observed: Crashes in Catalonia in which someone was killed or seriously injured, 2016–2023, on the roads the model covers. Each year was predicted by a model fitted only on the years before it, with its penalty, form, roads-through-towns rule and whether each province has a starting level of its own also chosen on those years alone. The crashes are split into ten equal groups by the model's prediction (about 1,161 crashes each), and separately by the table's. Each dot is the share of a group's crashes that were fatal (someone died within 24 hours), with its 95% interval, against the group's average prediction. Source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury. n = 11,611.
